c.tagline: Vietnam's beach-and-bridges city — My Khe sands, the Dragon Bridge, and a gateway to Hoi An.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis (Mai Linh, Vinasun) are reliable, but Grab and the electric Xanh SM are usually cheaper and remove any haggling over the fare.

emergency.note: 114 reaches the fire service. Operators may have limited English; hotel reception can help relay an emergency.

hood_landmark.Sơn Trà: Linh Ung Pagoda Son Tra Da Nang
hood_landmark.Thanh Khê: Da Nang city beach Nguyen Tat Thanh

avoid.reason: Motorbike bag- and phone-snatching occurs along the beach roads; keep phones away from the curb side.

hood_desc: The downtown core on the west bank of the Han River, home to the Dragon Bridge, Han Market, Da Nang Cathedral and the Cham Museum; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers who want the city's sights, cafes and riverfront at their doorstep.

The beachside tourist quarter behind My Khe Beach, packed with Western and Vietnamese restaurants, bars, spas, dive shops and co-working cafes; the go-to area for nightlife, dining and digital nomads.

The peninsula and eastern riverbank district, running from the Han River Bridge up to the Son Tra headland with Linh Ung Pagoda and the Lady Buddha statue; a quieter, upscale mix of beach resorts, seafood spots and sea views.

The southern coastal district around the Marble Mountains and Non Nuoc Beach, lined with luxury beach resorts and the marble-carving village; suits travelers who want landmark sightseeing paired with a resort-style stay.

A local, residential district on the northern city-beach side near the railway station; less touristy and better value, good for travelers who want an everyday-Vietnam feel within a short ride of downtown.
lodging: A La Carte Da Nang Beach
Hyatt Regency Danang Resort and Spa
Muong Thanh Luxury Song Han Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable for visitors.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 6:00 PM; there is no late-night public transit, so Grab, Xanh SM and taxis cover the evenings.
transit.note: Da Nang has no metro or tram; a network of public city buses serves the main corridors, but most visitors get around by Grab, Xanh SM (electric taxis/bikes), taxis and rented motorbikes.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor (around 5,000-20,000 VND depending on the route); there is no city-wide smartcard, and ride-hailing apps are paid in-app or in cash.

bus: Open-tour and sleeper buses to Hoi An, Hue, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City
train: Da Nang Railway Station (North-South Reunification line to Hue, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City)

transit.m: Grab or metered taxi to the city center (10-15 min)
Public city bus to downtown (limited routes, ~25 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service at tourist-facing restaurants and for spa or tour staff is appreciated.
